title: Maternal circulating cytokine and chemokine levels during pregnancy and risk of autism spectrum disorder in offspring: A systematic review and meta-analysis
title_zh: 孕期母体循环细胞因子与趋化因子水平与子代自闭症谱系障碍风险的系统综述与荟萃分析
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy has been implicated in offspring neurodevelopment, but evidence linking maternal gestational immune mediators with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remains heterogeneous. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether maternal circulating cytokine and chemokine levels during pregnancy are associated with autism in offspring. METHODS: Five databases were searched for human observational studies measuring maternal blood cytokines or chemokines during pregnancy and reporting autism outcomes in offspring. Eligible studies included autism versus control comparisons using maternal serum or plasma samples. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted using odds ratios (ORs) as the primary effect measure. Standardised mean differences (SMDs) were also analysed where group-level concentration data were available. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics, and small-study effects were explored using Egger's test where estimable. RESULTS: Seven studies met the eligibility criteria. In OR-based analyses, nominal associations with autism were observed for IL-10 (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.06-1.69), CXCL10 (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.24-2.11), IL-1α (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.23-1.65), IL-5 (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.18-1.89), and IL-17A (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.94). CCL4 showed a borderline association. Supportive SMD analyses indicated higher IL-6 and lower IL-1β concentrations in autism-associated pregnancies. Heterogeneity varied across analytes and was substantial for IL-10 and CCL4. CONCLUSION: Maternal gestational immune profiles may differ in pregnancies later associated with autism, but current evidence does not support a single robust cytokine biomarker. Progress requires larger prospective cohorts with repeated sampling, harmonised assays, pathway-level analyses, and integrated placental-foetal neurodevelopmental phenotyping.
abstract_zh: 背景：孕期母体免疫激活（MIA）已被认为与子代神经发育相关，但母体妊娠期免疫介质与自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）之间的关联证据仍不一致。本系统综述与荟萃分析评估了孕期母体循环细胞因子和趋化因子水平是否与子代自闭症相关。方法：检索五个数据库，纳入人类观察性研究，测量孕期母体血液细胞因子或趋化因子并报告子代自闭症结果。符合条件的研究包括使用母体血清或血浆样本的自闭症与对照组比较。采用随机效应模型进行荟萃分析，主要效应量为比值比（OR）。若有组级浓度数据，也分析标准化均值差（SMD）。使用I²统计量评估异质性，并在可估计时使用Egger检验探讨小样本效应。结果：七项研究符合纳入标准。在OR分析中，IL-10（OR 1.34，95% CI 1.06-1.69）、CXCL10（OR 1.62，95% CI 1.24-2.11）、IL-1α（OR 1.42，95% CI 1.23-1.65）、IL-5（OR 1.49，95% CI 1.18-1.89）与自闭症呈显著正相关，IL-17A（OR 0.81，95% CI 0.70-0.94）呈负相关。CCL4显示边缘性关联。SMD分析支持IL-6升高、IL-1β降低与自闭症相关的妊娠。不同分析物的异质性差异显著，IL-10和CCL4的异质性较大。结论：母体妊娠期免疫特征可能在后续与自闭症相关的妊娠中存在差异，但目前证据尚未支持单一稳健的细胞因子生物标志物。未来进展需要更大规模的前瞻性队列，重复采样，统一检测方法，通路层面分析，以及整合胎盘-胎儿神经发育表型。
